transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-05-28 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: Sophie, Martin, Priya (Redwood) + Daniel, Rosa, Arjun, Maya, Liam (Cobalt)

[00:00] Sophie Tran: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick sound check?
[00:06] Daniel Brooks: Yep good here.
[00:08] Rosa Vega: Can hear you Sophie.
[00:10] Sophie Tran: Great. Objective for today — do a short retrospective on the spike last week, walk through cost levers, and align on a short pilot to stabilize costs ahead of their summer campaign. Martin will jump into perf numbers.
[00:25] Martin Li: Hi all. Quick context — I pulled a sample of the production traces Arjun shared and ran a quick continuous-batching sim. Not exact repro but gives direction.
[00:34] Arjun Patel: Note, the traces were anonymized, we removed some user ids. hope that's okay for the bench.
[00:38] Martin Li: Totally fine. A couple high-level things: 1) the spike correlated with longer context prompts — mean input length jumped by ~3.5x, 2) we saw session stickiness so KV cache wasn't as effective as expected, and 3) there were several retries during the surge which amplified token counts.
[01:00] Rosa Vega: When you say retries, are those from client-side timeouts or internal queueing?
[01:05] Martin Li: Mostly client-side timeouts. Some were due to burst throttling on the hosted tier; we saw 429-like behavior when queue depth increased. Not huge but enough to cascade.
[01:16] Daniel Brooks: Right, our frontend default timeout's 2s and some requests are hitting up to 2.8s. We need to tune that.
[01:22] Priya Desai: That's a common pattern — timeouts cause retries and that raises cost. We call that the retry tax in the health playbook.
[01:29] Sophie Tran: Quick question for Maya on the finance side — is the main constraint fixed-month budget or monthly burn target?
[01:35] Maya Singh: For this quarter it's monthly burn; the execs want to keep avg MRR growth but cap variable spend until they see predictable savings. So they prefer a hybrid — hosted for ramp, Dedicated reserve if we can show 20-30% cost savings.
[01:48] Liam O'Connor: We also have regulatory notes — some PII flows require VPC routing; that's non-negotiable for a subset of traffic.
[01:55] Sophie Tran: Got it. We'll separate routing by policy. Martin, can you comment on Dedicated pool economics for their workload?
[02:02] Martin Li: Sure. Rough numbers from initial model: for their token distribution, a reserved Dedicated pool with autoscale saved about 22% vs hosted per-token in steady state. If we factor in long context prompts and enable prefix caching and quantization suggestions, we hit ~28-32% savings. But the win depends heavily on achievable cache hit rate and whether the model can be quantized without causing QA regressions.
[02:28] Daniel Brooks: About quantization — our evaluation team is sensitive to hallucination shifts. How do we monitor quality after quantization?
[02:34] Martin Li: We recommend running the Redwood Optimize eval harness — baseline set + targeted QA prompts. We'll instrument a regression alert pinned to the prompt set. If any metric drops beyond threshold, rollback is automatic.
[02:44] Rosa Vega: Can Redwood host the eval harness or do we need to run it?
[02:48] Sophie Tran: We can run it collaboratively. SEs can run an initial pass on staging; we can then hand over to your eval team.
[02:55] Arjun Patel: On the staging note — we still need SSO/SAML and a temporary VPC peering to route test traffic. I put that in the notes we sent.
[03:03] Priya Desai: We'll open a support ticket after this and attach the runbook for staging peering.

-- Topic shift: root cause and short-term mitigations --
[03:18] Daniel Brooks: Walk me through short-term fixes we can push in the next 48-72 hours.
[03:21] Martin Li: Immediate items: 1) increase client timeouts slightly or implement linear backoff to reduce retries, 2) enable prefix/KV cache on sessions where conversation fragments are shared, 3) deploy a soft rate limit on the client side to protect hosted tier during ramp. Those three together should lower the retry amplification and reduce token churn.
[03:40] Liam O'Connor: How intrusive is enabling KV cache? Will our clients need to change integration?
[03:44] Martin Li: Minimal SDK config change — it's mostly a header flag and optional state storage. We do recommend a brief integration test. The issue is consistent conversation IDs to key cache correctly.
[03:53] Arjun Patel: We can add a conversation id in the header, that's fine.
[03:57] Maya Singh: What's the expected delta in cost if we flip cache on for 60% of sessions?
[04:02] Martin Li: Ballpark: with your traffic shape, 60% cacheable sessions reduces token spend by ~18-25%. But again depends on prompt redundancy.

-- Mid-call: reliability incidents and SLA discussion --
[04:20] Rosa Vega: We had two brief blips where visible latency spiked to ~6s. Any chance this was region-related?
[04:26] Martin Li: The traces point to a temporary capacity imbalance in the hosted pool in us-west-2 during the spike window. Our runtime did route a subset to other regions but some pinning logic kept sessions in us-west-2. We can propose a failover policy change.
[04:39] Sophie Tran: For SLA, we can offer a canary routing policy that favours lower latency cross-region fallback for critical endpoints. That reduces region pinning risk at the cost of slight egress/regional differences.
[04:51] Daniel Brooks: Egress costs are manageable; latency matters more.
[04:54] Priya Desai: We'll include canary routing in the pilot scope and measure p95 latency and error rate as success criteria.

[05:05] Martin Li: Also noted — we should run a stress test on the staging VPC to validate autoscale thresholds and pre-warm pools. That reduces cold-start throttles.
[05:15] Arjun Patel: We'll give you a window early next week for staging ramp tests.

-- Pilot and evaluation criteria --
[05:25] Sophie Tran: Proposed pilot: 2-week pilot in staging, two routing lanes (PII -> Dedicated VPC; non-PII -> Hosted with caching), run baseline latency/cost tests, enable quantization on a control slice, collect quality metrics. Success = 20% reduction in per-token cost or p95 latency < 1.2s for 95% of traffic. Does that sound reasonable?
[05:47] Daniel Brooks: Yes sounds reasonable. We add one more: no QA drift > 1.5% on our hallucination metric.
[05:54] Martin Li: We can instrument that. We'll hook up automatic regression alerts to your Slack channel or a webhook.

[06:00] Maya Singh: From finance — if the pilot shows 25% savings, what's the typical committed pool term and discount?
[06:07] Sophie Tran: Typically 6-12 months for a mid-size reserved commit, discounts scale with commit size. Sophie: I'll send the pricing grid after the call.
[06:16] Maya Singh: Please do.

[06:20] Liam O'Connor: A couple security questions quick — data retention on logs, ability to purge, and KMS integration for in-flight keys.
[06:28] Martin Li: We support KMS integrations for private deployments; for hosted we offer customer-managed keys in select tiers. Logs can be set to a retention policy; we also offer token redaction at ingest. We'll attach SOC2 doc and a security whitepaper.
[06:42] Rosa Vega: We'll need the SOC2 and HSM/KMS specifics before any Dedicated commit.
[06:47] Priya Desai: Noted; I'll put that on the action list.

-- Closing and recap --
[06:55] Sophie Tran: Quick recap: action items are pricing sheet, staging VPC peering, SE benchmark run, and budget decision. Also we'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for the pilot next Tuesday. Any objections?
[07:06] Daniel Brooks: None. Thanks.
[07:08] Arjun Patel: Works for us.
[07:10] Maya Singh: I'll aim to have a budget window by 6/10.
[07:13] Sophie Tran: Great. We'll follow up with calendar invite and attach the security docs and runbook. Thanks everyone.
[07:18] Rosa Vega: Thanks all.
[07:20] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: background chatter cut a few lines, some product names transcribed odd (e.g., "Red wood dedicated"), timestamps approximate.
